title: Compression ↔ Intimacy — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Compression ↔ Intimacy's rich face, its first round at Sketch tier, a proposal. One synthetic voice, whisper to shout, runs all three pieces on one engine: for the technical side, the voice carried away in open air to test whether distance narrows a voice's range, then the page's own whisper-and-shout pair built; for the vulnerability parallel, the four knobs turned against the page's line for each, to the release line where they part; for the teaching, the page's Part 1 matched in loudness, with a close microphone's bass as the control, walked up to 24 blind pairs asking where the singer is. Advanced Applications has no piece: a parallel-compression blend on this voice would only confirm what the page already says it does, and its felt claim needs the same ear the blind test asks for. The Vulnerability Parallel is a ### heading, so its piece sits in The Conceptual Side and is approved with it. I grow when a listener's scores come back, or when a real vocal take can stand beside the synthetic one. I never hold the entry's words.

pieces.file: Compression ↔ Intimacy — rich — does distance narrow a voice.html
pieces.title: Does distance narrow a voice? · a whisper in your ear, a shout across a field
pieces.caption: **Does distance narrow a voice’s range, or widen it?** One synthetic phrase, a pulse and noise through formant filters, nobody recorded: whisper to shout, 32 dB from its quietest syllable to its loudest at 5 cm. Three steps. The phrase at the microphone. The singer carried away in open air to 50 m, with the test set before the slider moves: if a small range is what near sounds like, the range should widen with distance. It never does. Alone, the voice keeps its range to within 10⁻¹³ dB at every distance; over a quiet floor the whispers sink first and it narrows, 27.9 dB at 4 m, 12.2 at 32 m. Last, the page’s own pair built, a whisper in your ear and a shout across a field. What differs there is not range: the whisper arrives 27.4 dB louder though it was made 32 dB softer, the gap between effort and level that Brungart and Scott (JASA 110, 2001) found listeners use to judge distance. Rooms were tried and left out: across twelve rooms of one size the range at 8 m moved from −2.5 to +3.6 dB, by each room’s colour, not by distance.
pieces.near: Our ears interpret small dynamic range as proximity

pieces.file: Compression ↔ Intimacy — rich — four knobs and the guard.html
pieces.title: Four knobs and the guard · the vulnerability parallel, measured
pieces.caption: **Which way does the hold point?** The 4:1 voice from the blind test below, with its gain reduction drawn under it, then each knob turned against the page’s line for it. Threshold: below it nothing is held; at −30 dB it touches 4 of 7 syllables, at −10 none. Ratio: 1:1 holds nothing; ∞:1 pins the shout to the threshold, −30.1 dB. Attack: at 50 ms the shout’s start stands 8.2 dB above its held part, at 1 ms 2.3. Those three lines read the hold as the guard. Last, release, the test, set before the slider moves: on that same reading a slow release keeps the guard up, and the page says it keeps you open. Measured: at 1 s the soft line after the shout is held 11.0 dB where its own level asks 1.8, the whisper after it 7.0, and the extra hold lasts 1.38 s; at 40 ms, 1.9 dB, 0.0 and 79 ms. The release line holds only if the hold is the closeness, which is how the page’s opening and its Part 3 read compression. The Vulnerability Parallel is a ### heading, so this piece sits in, and is approved with, The Conceptual Side.

pieces.file: Compression ↔ Intimacy — rich — where is the singer.html
pieces.title: Where is the singer? · Part 1, blind, with a control
pieces.caption: **Where is the singer, when only the range changes?** Part 1 on a synthetic voice: uncompressed, 4:1 (threshold −30 dB, 10 and 120 ms) and 20:1 (−44 dB, 1 and 40 ms), each matched to −20 LUFS by BS.1770-4 gated loudness measured in the piece; and a fourth, the uncompressed voice through a cardioid’s proximity effect at 5 cm (+7.7 dB at 200 Hz against 1 kHz), the control that tells range from spectral tilt. Four steps walk up to 24 blind pairs, eight for each version against the uncompressed one, order and side random, asking which singer is closer. The rule is set before the first pair: 7 or 8 of 8 reads closer (1 in 28 by guessing), 0 or 1 farther, and the page’s claim is read from the 4:1 set alone. Leaks checked and printed: equal length and start; inside each syllable the compressor changes level, not colour (0.14 dB at most), while the shelf lifts below 300 Hz by 4.7 to 8.1 dB; the 20:1 gain moves 0.62 dB inside the held shout (residue −47 dB) and, looking 5 ms ahead, adds no click at the onsets. Three can’t be closed, and the piece says so: no match holds every reading of level (the uncompressed voice’s loudest 400 ms are 2.9 dB above the 20:1’s, its average 2.9 dB below); raising the breathy whispers brightens the phrase (+7.2 dB above 3 kHz at 4:1); and a listener who can hear which one is compressed can answer the page instead of the singer. Whether 20:1 sounds fake is not scored. No listener has taken it yet.

offers.what: “A whispered voice in your ear has minimal range; a shout across a field has enormous range” doesn’t hold as physics, measured on the piece “does distance narrow a voice”. Distance in open air takes the same dB from every syllable: a 32 dB phrase keeps 32 dB from 5 cm to 50 m (largest change 7×10⁻¹⁴ dB over 61 distances; 0.001 would have failed). Over a quiet floor the range narrows, never widens (27.87 dB at 4 m, 12.17 at 32 m). Across twelve rooms the range at 8 m moved −2.5 to +3.6 dB, mean +0.5, by room colour. The page’s own pair, built, differs in effort against arrival level, not range: the whisper in your ear arrives 27.4 dB louder than the shout across the field, though made 32 dB softer. That gap is a known distance cue: Brungart & Scott 2001, JASA 110(1):425–440, doi 10.1121/1.1379730 (abstract read, full text not): for high-level voiced speech, judged distance doubled with each 8 dB rise in production level and each 12 dB fall in presentation level. Suggested: “Our ears hear distance partly in the gap between how hard a voice was made and how loud it arrives: a whisper that arrives loud can only be close. A compressor with makeup gain lifts the quiet syllables into that gap.” Whether the whole voice sounds closer, the sentence’s perceptual half, stays open on a listener’s score in the blind test under Teaching the Resonance. The same reading recurs in Common Student Discoveries: “near-zero range simulates centimeters of distance”.

The Vulnerability Parallel’s release line runs against its own other three lines, measured on the piece “four knobs and the guard”. Threshold, ratio and attack read gain reduction as the guard: no hold is “safe to be authentic”, ∞:1 is “complete guard up”, a fast attack is “immediate defense”. On that reading a slow release keeps the guard up after the moment passes: at 1 s the soft line after the shout is held 11.0 dB where its own level asks 1.8, the whisper after it 7.0 dB, and the extra hold lasts 1.38 s; at 40 ms, 1.9 dB, 0.0 dB and 79 ms. The page says “Slow release: Stay open longer” and “Fast release: Quickly return to protected state”, which is true only if the hold is the closeness, as the page’s opening and Part 3 read it (“Amount of compression = amount of intimacy”). Two ways home, Loudon’s choice: keep the guard reading and turn the release line (“Release = how long the guard stays up after the moment passes. Fast release: back to open quickly. Slow release: guarded long after.”), or name the double reading as a contradiction the page holds: the compressor is both the guard and the closeness.

The table mixes the same two readings the Conceptual Side offer names. “Reduces loud peaks | Reduces defensive reactions”, “Creates proximity effect | Creates emotional closeness” and “Slow release = sustain | Sustained openness = deep connection” read the compressor as the closeness; “Controlled by threshold | Controlled by trust” and “Fast attack = guarded | Quick defense = guarded” read its hold as the guard. Measured on “four knobs and the guard”: a slow release keeps the hold on (11.0 dB on the soft line after the shout at 1 s, 1.9 at 40 ms). Carry with the Conceptual Side offer; whichever way that one goes, this table follows.
